old.claim: On an overlap write $X=Y\circ T$. The transition is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of open subsets of $\mathbb R^2$. F4 gives $DX=(DY\circ T)DT$ and hence $J_X=(J_Y\circ T)|\det DT|$, with $J_X=\sqrt{\det(DX^TDX)}$. The regularity makes both Gram densities positive. F3 transfers each continuously weighted integral whose support is compact inside that overlap between its two coordinate descriptions.

proposed.claim: For graph charts $X:U_X\to S\cap O_X$ and $Y:U_Y\to S\cap O_Y$, put $E=S\cap O_X\cap O_Y$, $V=X^{-1}(E)$ and $W=Y^{-1}(E)$. These parameter domains are open, and $T=Y^{-1}\circ X:V\to W$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism with $X=Y\circ T$. F4 gives $DX=(DY\circ T)DT$ and hence $J_X=(J_Y\circ T)|\det DT|$, with $J_X=\sqrt{\det(DX^TDX)}$; rank two makes both Gram densities positive. Let $w:S\to\mathbb R$ be continuous with compact support $C\subset E$. The function $p(z)=w(Y(z))J_Y(z)$ on $W$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^2$, is continuous with support contained in the compact set $Y^{-1}(C)\subset W=T(V)$, so it is Riemann integrable by F5. Apply F3 with $n=2$ and this $T,p$. Its pulled-back integrand on $V$ is $w(X(y))J_X(y)$, so the two zero-extended coordinate integrals agree.
